messages.author: 1e1f6c27d3c442a5
messages.subject: reactivity if/actionButton (bug?)
parts:
Hi,

here is a strange beahviour obtained with actionButton and if statement in reactivity :

=======ui.R===========
shinyUI(basicPage(
    actionButton("button1","1"),
    actionButton("button2","2"),
    textOutput("what_is_pressed")
 ))


What works not well :

=======server.R========
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    
    button1_calls <- 0
    button2_calls <- 0
    
    output$what_is_pressed <- renderText({        
        if(button1_calls < input$button1) {
            button1_calls <<- input$button1
            return("Button 1")
        }
        if(button2_calls < input$button2) {
            button2_calls <<- input$button2
            return("Button 2")
        }
    })
})

A simple turn-around is to add explicitly
input$button1
input$button2
before the if statements :

=======server.R========
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    
    button1_calls <- 0
    button2_calls <- 0
    
    output$what_is_pressed <- renderText({
        input$button1
        input$button2
        
        if(button1_calls < input$button1) {
            button1_calls <<- input$button1
            return("Button 1")
        }
        if(button2_calls < input$button2) {
            button2_calls <<- input$button2
            return("Button 2")
        }
    })
})


I think it should be considered as a bug, but I am not sure...

Best,

Yann

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: reactivity if/actionButton (bug?)
parts:
You're encountering a subtlety in how Shiny tracks dependencies between reactive components. The short version is that, in the first version of the code, after you click button1 so input$button1 is incremented, the renderText() returns before ever evaluating input$button2, so it stops tracking changes to input$button2.

What you want is for output$what_is_pressed to depend on input$button2. Each time the renderText for output$what_is_pressed runs, the reactive dependencies are cleared; as it runs the code and reaches another reactive component, it takes a dependency on that component. When it evaluates input$button1, the output object takes a dependency on input$button1 -- but then your code returns immediately (when button1_calls < input$button1) so it never reaches input$button2 and takes a dependency on that.

In summary, the dependency structure of the reactive components is cleared and created each time the code is executed -- Shiny doesn't scan the code ahead of time to track dependency structure.

See these sections of the tutorial for more information:
  http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview
  http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#execution-scheduling

-Winston

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reactivity if/actionButton (bug?)
parts:
I would recommend this construction instead:

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
    
    values <- reactiveValues(lastPressed = NULL)

    observe({
        if (input$button1 > 0)
            values$lastPressed <- "Button 1"
    })

    observe({
        if (input$button2 > 0)
            values$lastPressed <- "Button 2"
    })
    
    output$what_is_pressed <- renderText({        
        values$lastPressed
    })
})
